note: A single-edged sword with a blade suited to cutting.
A recurring character in H. P. Lovecraft’s fiction, including The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath, in which he seeks a marvelous city glimpsed in dreams.

sources.label: H. P. Lovecraft: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath

short: A threshold of Lovecraft’s dream realm.
note: The gate reached by descending seven hundred steps in H. P. Lovecraft’s The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath; beyond it lies the Enchanted Wood.

sources.label: H. P. Lovecraft: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath

short: The enchanted sword in a Lord Dunsany tale.
note: The magical sword wielded by Leothric in Lord Dunsany’s “The Fortress Unvanquishable, Save for Sacnoth” (1908), able to overcome an otherwise impregnable fortress.

sources.label: Lord Dunsany: The Fortress Unvanquishable, Save for Sacnoth

short: A visitor to Lovecraft’s uncanny hilltop house.
note: The philosopher who visits a mysterious house above Kingsport in H. P. Lovecraft’s “The Strange High House in the Mist” (1926).

sources.label: H. P. Lovecraft: The Strange High House in the Mist

note: A fictional Massachusetts coastal town in H. P. Lovecraft’s fiction, including “The Strange High House in the Mist.”

sources.label: H. P. Lovecraft: The Strange High House in the Mist

note: A horse-drawn cab whose driver sits high behind the enclosed passenger compartment.

short: A devil’s name meaning “lord of flies.”
note: A biblical name for the devil, derived from a Hebrew title meaning “lord of flies,” originally the name of a Philistine god.
